facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held on 12 March 2011 in Baku.
According to the applicant, the demonstration was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstration was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration on 12 March 2011 in Baku.
Shortly after the demonstration had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the police dispersal operation.
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of the rules on holding public assemblies).
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).

By a decision of 12 March 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to eight days' administrative detention by its decision of 12 March 2011.

By a decision of 12 April 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention by its decision of 12 April 2011.
On the day of the applicant's arrest, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was drawn up in respect of the applicant by police officer E.G.
The administrative-offence report stated that at around 2.55 p.m. on 12 March 2011, at Fountains Square in Baku, the applicant had attempted to hold an unlawful demonstration.
The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order of a police officer.
According to the applicant, his name — the eleventh on the list in the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A. — was added to the report later in different handwriting.
According to the official records, the administrative-offence report in the applicant's respect was prepared on the basis of the report drawn up by police officers M.A. and H.A.
According to the applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents from his case file.

At the material time, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise himself with the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative-offence report.
The administrative-offence report stated that at around 2.55 p.m. on 12 March 2011, at Fountains Square in Baku, the applicant had attempted to hold an unlawful demonstration.
The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order of a police officer.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration at the place indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) proposed a different location for the demonstration on the outskirts of Baku — the grounds of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstration in the centre of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the originally indicated location.
Shortly after the demonstration had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the police dispersal operation.
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (violation of the rules on holding public assemblies).
The applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest.
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer while he was in police custody.
A State-funded lawyer was appointed to assist the applicant before the Sabail District Court.
None of the material submitted to the Court contains any record showing that the State-funded lawyer, Mr E.N., made any oral submissions on behalf of the applicant.
None of the material submitted to the Court contains any record showing that the State-funded lawyer, Mr E.N., made any written submissions on behalf of the applicant.
No witnesses were questioned during the court hearing before the Sabail District Court on 12 March 2011.

By a decision of 12 March 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to eight days' administrative detention by its decision of 12 March 2011.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to summon and examine witness Mr A.H., who, according to the applicant, had witnessed his arrest and time in custody.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to summon and examine witness Mr A.M., who, according to the applicant, had witnessed his arrest and time in custody.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to summon and examine witness Mr R.M., who, according to the applicant, had witnessed his arrest and time in custody.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to examine the video recordings made by Mr A.H., which, according to the applicant, showed his arrest and custody in the police stations.

The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to order a handwriting examination of the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A., in order to establish whether his name had been added to it by one of those two police officers.
The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the applicant's requests to summon and examine witnesses Mr A.H., Mr A.M. and Mr R.M. on his behalf.
The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the applicant's request to examine the video recordings made by Mr A.H.
According to the applicant, during the re-examination of the case he was not given an opportunity to appoint a lawyer of his own choosing.
A State-funded lawyer was appointed to assist the applicant during the re-examination of the case before the Sabail District Court on 12 April 2011.
The only witnesses questioned during the re-examination hearing before the Sabail District Court on 12 April 2011 were police officers M.A. and E.G.

Police officer M.A. testified at the re-examination hearing that the applicant had been detained for having participated in an unlawful assembly, making noise and disobeying the lawful orders of the police.
Police officer E.G. testified at the re-examination hearing that he had prepared the administrative-offence report in respect of the applicant.

By a decision of 12 April 2011, the Sabail District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer).
The Sabail District Court sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention by its decision of 12 April 2011.
The applicant requested that witness Mr A.H. be summoned and heard before the Baku Court of Appeal during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The applicant requested that witness Mr A.M. be summoned and heard before the Baku Court of Appeal during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The applicant requested that witness Mr R.M. be summoned and heard before the Baku Court of Appeal during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The applicant requested that witness Mr R.B. be summoned and heard before the Baku Court of Appeal during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The applicant challenged the reliability of the official records related to his arrest and police custody before the Baku Court of Appeal during the second set of appeal proceedings.

The applicant pointed out a discrepancy between the time of arrest indicated in the administrative-offence report (around 2.55 p.m.) and the time indicated in the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A. (around 4 p.m.).

The applicant repeated his allegation before the Baku Court of Appeal that his name had been added as the eleventh person on the list in the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A. later and in different handwriting.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to hear at least three individuals listed along with him in the report prepared by police officers M.A. and H.A.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to examine certain photographs made during his arrest and time in police custody.
The applicant asked the Baku Court of Appeal to examine video recordings made during his arrest and time in police custody.
The applicant was not represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the applicant's requests to summon and hear witnesses Mr A.H., Mr A.M., Mr R.M. and Mr R.B. during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the applicant's request to examine photographs during the second set of appeal proceedings.
The Baku Court of Appeal did not address the applicant's request to examine video recordings during the second set of appeal proceedings.
